violations.text: The Person in charge did not assure compliance with critical code requirements. New Violation. Correct By: 08/12/2026

Dishes, rags, aprons, and a coat were observed in the hand-washing sink on the cook line, a sponge and food debris was observed in the hand-washing sink at the sushi bar, rags and a chemical spray bottle were hanging on the splash guard of the bar hand washing sinks. utensils were observed in the hand-washing sink. A hand-washing sink must not be used for purposes other than hand washing. All items were removed. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026

Molluscan shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026

Molluscan Shellfish (clams) located in the walk-in freezer did not have the proper identification tags. Molluscan Shellstock tags must remain attached to the container in which the Molluscan Shellstock are received until the container is empty. Tags were on shelf in kitchen; PIC placed with clams in freezer. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (can opener, ice machine) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Can opener was brought to dishwasher, ice machine taken out of service. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026

The chlorine sanitizer concentration for the sanitizing cycle of the dishwasher was 0 parts per million (ppm). Chlorine sanitizing solutions must be between 50-100 ppm. PIC changed chemical bottle. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026

The quaternary ammonium concentration in the sanitizing solution of the 3-bay sink was 0 parts per million (ppm). According to the manufacturer's use directions, the concentration of the quaternary ammonium must be 200 ppm. PIC drained sink and refilled with sanitizer. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026
Herbed butter was observed at 64 degrees F on the spice cart. PIC moved to refrigeration. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026

Several foods were observed held at 45-56 degrees Fahrenheit in the prep units. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Foods requiring refrigeration were disposed. Other foods moved to alternate refrigeration. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026
TPHC logs for sushi rice were unavailable for review at the time of this inspection. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026

Working containers of spices and sauces are not labeled with the common name of the food. Working containers holding food or food ingredients that are removed from their original packages, such as flour, herbs, salt, sugar, and spices must be labeled with the common name of the food. New Violation. Correct By: 08/12/2026
Buckets of soup and noodles were observed stored on the floor in the wok area. Food must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. New Violation. Correct By: 08/12/2026
Knives were stored between prep units and on an unclean hook. PIC removed. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/29/2026

The non-food contact surfaces of the following have an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris:-under prep unit hoods-spice cart shelves-refrigerator gaskets-multiple refrigeration doors-cooking equipment. New Violation. Correct By: 08/12/2026

The floors and walls under and behind equipment in the kitchen, under dry storage shelving, and walk-in freezer floor have an accumulation of soil residue and/or food debris. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 08/12/2026

Unnecessary and/or non-functional equipment or items were observed in the rear entry hall area. Establishments shall be kept free of unnecessary and/or non-functional equipment and litter to prevent harborage conditions. New Violation. Correct By: 08/26/2026

An open employees' beverage container was observed stored in a food preparation area. Employees shall not drink from open beverage containers in order to prevent contamination of their hands, the container, and exposed food. Covers were placed on beverages. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/25/2025

Establishment is not documenting the amount disposed and time of disposal for sushi rice as required. Inspector instructed staff and PIC during inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/25/2025
Eggrolls were observed stored in a reused box. Staff removed and placed in container. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/25/2025
Utensils were observed stored in stagnant water between uses. A knife was observed stored between prep units. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/25/2025
